query: How was ARDL used to test the nexus, and what long-run association did it reveal for human capital and renewable energy?
final_answer: The clearest evidence shows that ARDL was used in a China-based study to test the nexus among variables after first checking stationarity with the augmented Dickey-Fuller test, and the same study covered data from 1986–2019 [https://openalex.org/W4313181844||ABSTRACT||000]. In that analysis, ARDL results indicated that human capital, renewable energy consumption, and renewable energy production were negatively associated with carbon emissions and positively associated with sustainable development goals [https://openalex.org/W4313181844||ABSTRACT||000]. A related China study also used ARDL, together with ADF and Granger causality, to evaluate associations and directional nexus over 1986–2019, but it did not mention human capital, so it cannot be used to specify a human-capital/renewable-energy long-run result [https://openalex.org/W4315784444||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers in the set used variants or related models such as CS-ARDL, nonlinear ARDL, and dynamic ARDL simulations, but their abstracts either focused on different variables or did not report a human-capital-specific long-run association with renewable energy [https://openalex.org/W4388450586||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4206606027||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4315629505||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports that ARDL was used as a nexus-testing framework in at least one empirical study, but the provided summaries do not separately report a distinct long-run estimate specifically for the relationship between human capital and renewable energy [https://openalex.org/W4313181844||ABSTRACT||000]. Thus, the long-run implication available from the summaries is only the broader positive association of human capital and renewable energy variables with sustainable development outcomes and their negative association with carbon emissions, rather than a standalone human-capital-renewable-energy coefficient [https://openalex.org/W4313181844||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the context of Sustainable Consumption, what did the systematic review conclude about the concept’s complexity, its relationship to the circular economy, and the role of government in supporting sustainable consumption?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, sustainable consumption is presented as a complex and still-developing concept rather than a single, settled idea, with one review explicitly calling it a “complex and nebulous concept” whose theoretical fragmentation creates overlapping concepts [https://openalex.org/W4381591906||ABSTRACT||000]. Related reviews reinforce this complexity by showing that sustainability indicators for the circular economy are incomplete, that simple circularity metrics are insufficient, and that assessment must consider multiple dimensions rather than circularity alone [https://openalex.org/W3163949760||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3120864615||ABSTRACT||000]. The relationship between sustainable consumption and the circular economy is consistently portrayed as close and important, but also difficult: one review links consumers directly to the circular economy while noting the challenges of that interaction [https://openalex.org/W4381591906||ABSTRACT||000], and others describe the circular economy as an emerging field with limited theory and research, contested visions, and technocentric tendencies that can overlook social and ecological implications [https://openalex.org/W4211051495||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378216524||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers also caution that circularity does not automatically equal sustainability, because some “sustainable” practices may still harm environment or society, and increased circularity can create unintended externalities [https://openalex.org/W3132132623||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3120864615||ABSTRACT||000]. On the question of government, the systematic review literature indicates that government matters as part of the support structure for sustainable consumption, including its role and tools in the discussion of the concept [https://openalex.org/W4381591906||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers are more specific that sustainable circular transitions require collaboration among businesses, governments, and stakeholders, and that without policy steer and public support, the transition may fail to achieve sustainable outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4409544928||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4289130621||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the literature converges on the view that sustainable consumption is inherently interdisciplinary, tightly linked to circular economy debates, and dependent on government involvement, but it also shows that the field remains theoretically fragmented and empirically underdeveloped [https://openalex.org/W4381591906||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4211051495||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: In men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA), elevated FSH is associated with poorer sperm retrieval outcomes, and failed retrieval is also linked to elevated LH, whereas successful retrieval is linked to larger testicular volume, a higher testosterone-to-LH ratio, and bilateral testicular volumes as significant predictors in multivariate analysis [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000]. In the subgroup of men with NOA and chromosomal anomalies, Klinefelter syndrome (KS) is characterized by lower average testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, greater height and arm span, higher LH and FSH, and more frequent gynecomastia [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, men with testicular XX DSD show LH, FSH, and penile length values intermediate between the KS and undefined-cause groups, with testicular volume similar to the KS group but other data similar to the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study concludes that clinical and laboratory data can distinguish men with NOA and chromosomal anomalies, especially KS and testicular XX, from those with undefined causes [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the provided evidence does not give subgroup-specific FSH-outcome data for KS versus testicular XX DSD beyond these comparative baseline findings [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Another paper in this set addresses chromosomal abnormalities and AZF screening indications in NOA/severe oligozoospermia but does not report FSH-related clinical findings or KS/testicular XX DSD comparisons [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How do Sustainable Catalytric Technologies support global resource securty and sustainability?
final_answer: Sustainable Catalytric Technologies are presented across these papers as a way to support global resource security and sustainability by reducing dependence on fossil resources, scarce catalysts, and linear resource use patterns [https://openalex.org/W4397002662||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4401191227||ABSTRACT||000]. Several summaries frame catalysis as central to solving interconnected challenges such as climate change, pollution, and sustainable energy, with heterogeneous catalysis described as a key enabler of a sustainable future [https://openalex.org/W3136963614||ABSTRACT||000]. The papers also emphasize that catalyzed chemical transformations powered by renewable electricity can replace fossil fuels without reducing human wellbeing, while electrocatalytic processes can produce solar fuels and commodity chemicals for many sectors [https://openalex.org/W4323925755||ABSTRACT||000]. Resource security is further supported by biomass conversion and waste valorization, which can turn biomass into biofuels and high-value products and help shift industry from a linear to a circular economy [https://openalex.org/W4377108088||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4397002662||ABSTRACT||000]. In addition, rational design of earth-abundant catalysts is highlighted as a response to catalyst scarcity, and catalyst design best practices are presented as a way to improve sustainable product development [https://openalex.org/W4401191227||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3214828424||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also links these technologies to long-term system change, arguing that early action is needed to catalyze broader sustainability transitions and meet more ambitious targets by 2050 and 2100 [https://openalex.org/W4284690057||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the papers caution that technical, economic, and societal tradeoffs, as well as infrastructure, feedstock mobilization, techno-economics, and carbon-stock concerns, affect feasibility and acceptance [https://openalex.org/W4323925755||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4385888760||ABSTRACT||000]. Green chemistry and green engineering principles, together with quantitative sustainability analysis, are presented as tools for measuring improvements, identifying remaining problem areas, and guiding research investment and commercialization [https://openalex.org/W3156019499||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3156019499||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the papers agree that sustainable catalysis can help secure essential fuels, chemicals, and services while lowering environmental burdens, but they also show that real-world sustainability depends on careful assessment of tradeoffs and broader system conditions [https://openalex.org/W4397002662||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4323925755||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3156019499||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
final_answer: In the district-heating sustainability assessment study, five multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA, using 8 criteria for 12 district heating companies [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The paper reports that sensitivity analysis was used to identify the most credible method by changing criteria weights in three ways: varying them individually across the stability range of alternatives, varying them individually by a fixed amount to examine effects on average scores, and comparing AHP-derived weights with equal weights [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The study and its literature review concluded that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analyses of district heating systems, but they differ in their calculation procedures and in how their results are interpreted [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. This implies that method choice is not about whether the methods can be used at all, but about which one best fits the decision context and how its outputs should be read [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Broader sustainability-assessment literature is consistent with this contextual view, arguing that MCDA methods should be tailored to the decision situation and that method selection should be guided by methodological features [https://openalex.org/W4311545548||ABSTRACT||000]. Separately, a district-heating sustainability review found MCDM methods were preferred in practice and that AHP was the most frequently used method, but it did not provide the same kind of cross-method sensitivity comparison [https://openalex.org/W4315708900||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Based on the review of "sustainable innovations," what factors are said to encourage or block farmers" adoption of these innovations, and how do environmental values, in contrast with complexity, innovation aversion, and low perceived control, shape this adoption behavior?
final_answer: Across the reviews, farmers’ adoption of sustainable innovations is described as being encouraged by a mix of innovation characteristics, producer and operation characteristics, and broader social/institutional supports, while being blocked by attributes of the innovation and by farmers’ perceptions and beliefs [https://openalex.org/W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4210468156||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4309605934||ABSTRACT||001]. Specifically, adoption is fostered by factors such as specific innovation characteristics, self-efficacy, social-environmental altruism, communication and networking, other conservation practice use, cash-crop diversity, livestock operations, and farming size [https://openalex.org/W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387228452||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387228452||ABSTRACT||001]. It is also supported by producer demographics, land tenure, labor and credit availability, participation in demonstration trials, and access to policy frameworks, credit, research, extension services, and consumer demand for sustainably produced food [https://openalex.org/W4210468156||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3174938154||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4383033841||ABSTRACT||002]. In contrast, the review of sustainable innovations identifies innovation complexity, a high degree of innovation aversion, and low perceived control as major barriers to adoption [https://openalex.org/W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. Another review similarly argues that adoption is difficult to predict because technology attributes interact with dissemination institutions and farm/farmer-specific variables, and that complexity across sustainable practices can block or complicate adoption [https://openalex.org/W3118303193||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387228452||ABSTRACT||000]. Environmental values appear to encourage adoption: the review explicitly says environmental values can drive adoption, and it gives organic farmers as an example of actors with a stronger environmental view who place less weight on economic gains [https://openalex.org/W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, this suggests that environmental values can counterbalance barriers such as complexity, innovation aversion, and low perceived control by making farmers more willing to adopt sustainable innovations despite immediate economic tradeoffs [https://openalex.org/W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, one meta-analysis notes that methodological factors significantly affect willingness-to-accept estimates, reminding us that some reported adoption evidence is sensitive to study design rather than only substantive determinants [https://openalex.org/W4313535119||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What factors drive or bar farmers" adoption of sustainable innnovations, according to the review?
final_answer: Across the reviews, farmers’ adoption of sustainable innovations is shaped by a mix of economic, institutional, technological, psychological, and social factors, rather than by farmer characteristics alone [W3118303193||ABSTRACT||000][W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. Repeatedly identified drivers include education, extension and training, credit, income, irrigation, and soil quality, all of which are linked to higher adoption of sustainable technologies and practices [W4224306469||ABSTRACT||001]. Other reviews emphasize that adoption is also promoted when innovations have clear economic gains, social viability, technical feasibility, mitigable environmental risks, and access to efficient input and output markets [W4213433316||ABSTRACT||001]. Policy frameworks, research and extension services, and access to credit and resources for smallholder farmers are likewise described as important supports, while consumer awareness and demand for sustainably produced food can further incentivize adoption [W4383033841||ABSTRACT||002]. At the innovation level, adoption is encouraged by favorable innovation characteristics and by environmental values, with organic farmers tending to place more emphasis on environmental concerns and less on economic gains [W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. In contrast, key barriers include innovation complexity, innovation aversion, and low perceived control over the innovation [W4385875829||ABSTRACT||000]. Several reviews also stress that adoption is not a simple yes/no decision, because farmers may adopt partly, adaptively, or over time in different ways, which helps explain why adoption patterns are heterogeneous and hard to predict [W4387228452||ABSTRACT||000][W3118303193||ABSTRACT||000]. Methodological choices in the evidence base matter too: meta-analytic and SEM-focused reviews note that willingness-to-adopt estimates and model explanatory power are affected by methodological factors and by the selection of constructs such as attitude, subjective norms, and knowledge [W4313535119||ABSTRACT||000][W4309605934||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the reviews agree that promotion efforts should be tailored to local agricultural and dissemination contexts, and that better outcomes likely depend on aligning technology design, institutions, and farmer needs [W4224306469||ABSTRACT||001][W3118303193||ABSTRACT||000][W4309605934||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What did the interviews with retailers and service providers in North America reveal about managing product returns sustainably?
final_answer: The interviews with retailers and service providers in North America showed that firms were paying attention to the financial impact of product returns, but they had little awareness of the scale of returns’ environmental impacts [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000]. They also revealed that retailers lacked a comprehensive approach to managing the environmental impact of returns, which the authors identified as a barrier to developing sustainability plans for returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. A related interview-based study likewise found obstacles to sustainable reverse supply chains, including low incentives for RE producers to compete and a lack of governmental support for sustainable supply chain solutions [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, these papers suggest that sustainable returns management was constrained less by awareness of financial costs than by weak environmental understanding, fragmented planning, and external system barriers [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001]. Based on these findings, the authors proposed strategies and a framework to help retailers reduce the environmental impact of returns more sustainably [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence provided here does not specify which particular strategies were tested or how broadly the interviews represented North American retail and service sectors [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the public sector related to corporate governance, and what did the study say was stopping sustainable procurement in the Nigerian public construction sector?
final_answer: Across the supplied papers, the public sector is portrayed as important to sustainability and procurement because it is tied to policy, regulation, government support, and implementation conditions in Nigeria [https://openalex.org/W4308695771||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W3145060410||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper explicitly states that corporate governance is valuable and important in the public sector and links it to the sustainability of modern organisations, with governance understood through stakeholder management, ownership-management separation, governance structures, boards, and manager-board relationships [https://openalex.org/W10420025||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers do not directly connect the public sector to corporate governance, but they do reinforce that public-sector sustainability depends on institutional and regulatory conditions, including stronger policy frameworks and leadership support [https://openalex.org/W4220971596||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4386268572||ABSTRACT||000]. For the Nigerian public construction sector specifically, the study said sustainable procurement was being stopped by the absence of a sustainable procurement regulatory framework, lack of government commitment, poor economic conditions, and a lack of knowledge [https://openalex.org/W4308695771||ABSTRACT||000]. It also grouped barriers into attitude and poor fiscal incentive, financial restrictions, insufficient leadership and knowledge, and regulatory constraints, which is consistent with the broader emphasis on policy and capability gaps [https://openalex.org/W4308695771||ABSTRACT||000]. Related studies on sustainable construction in Nigeria similarly identified poor sustainability education, lack of incentives, ignorance of lifecycle cost benefits, low priority given to sustainability, and resistance to cultural change as major barriers [https://openalex.org/W3145060410||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that public-sector sustainability efforts are constrained less by a single factor than by a cluster of governance, regulatory, financial, and knowledge-related barriers [https://openalex.org/W4308695771||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3145060410||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How can the Paris Agreement be used in makin�27 healthcare or manufacturing teams push more sustainable practices, and what do the three I's say about why policy coherence with it can be helped or hindered?
final_answer: The Paris Agreement can be used as a policy reference point or target to push healthcare and manufacturing teams toward more sustainable practices by aligning their work with emissions reduction, climate-fighting goals, and broader sustainability ambitions [https://openalex.org/W4313495531||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000]. In healthcare, the evidence says decarbonising care should be paired with reducing disease incidence and severity, and Health in All Policies supports systematic intersectoral policymaking that minimizes environmental impacts on population health [https://openalex.org/W3128473151||ABSTRACT||002]. The healthcare-focused evidence also links sustainability with stronger social determinants of health, suggesting policy coherence is helped when Paris-aligned climate goals are connected to health, equity, and environmental protections [https://openalex.org/W3128473151||ABSTRACT||002]. For manufacturing and industry, the evidence points to choosing safer and more sustainable alternatives, implementing official guidelines to reduce carbon footprint, and using transformation policies to attract investment into safe and sustainable products and production methods [https://openalex.org/W4312064827||ABSTRACT||001]. More generally, the Paris Agreement and related global agendas can shape policy options, the ambition attached to sustainability goals, and the importance given to different actors and agendas, even though sector-specific examples are limited in the supplied evidence [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412423688||ABSTRACT||000]. The three I’s are ideas, institutions, and interests, and they can help policy coherence when they support coherence through the policy process, but hinder it when vested interests or ideologies work against it [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How does the review link green nanotechnology with environmental remediation in agro-ecosystems, and why does it say biogenic nanoparticles matter for this?
final_answer: Across the reviews, green nanotechnology is linked to agro-ecosystem remediation as a sustainability-oriented toolbox for agriculture and environmental restoration, rather than as a purely industrial materials field [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers describe nano-enabled agricultural functions such as nanosensors, nanofertilizers, nanopesticides, fungicides, biosensors, and nano-remediators that can improve crop productivity, monitor soil or pollutant conditions, and reduce reliance on excessive chemical inputs [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225104982||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000]. Others extend this to broader environmental remediation goals, including pollution management, water treatment, and incorporation into conventional remediation techniques for a holistic restoration strategy in agro-ecosystems [https://openalex.org/W4410647264||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4403849839||ABSTRACT||000]. The reviews agree that the appeal of the green approach is that it is framed as eco-friendly and supportive of sustainable agriculture, food security, and improved crop protection while minimizing environmental harm [https://openalex.org/W4380075578||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402449485||ABSTRACT||000]. Biogenic nanoparticles matter in this framing because the reviews repeatedly contrast biological or green synthesis with physical and chemical production methods that are said to be less economical, less sustainable, or more damaging to ecosystems [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4380075578||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000]. They are therefore presented as novel, biocompatible, cost-effective, and eco-friendly materials derived from plants, microbes, fungi, or their metabolites, making them suitable for sustainable farming and remediation applications [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225104982||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, one review cautions that practical deployment still faces unresolved issues such as scalability, control over nanoparticle properties, source variability, ecotoxicological uncertainty, toxicity assessment, and the need for regulatory frameworks and standardized protocols [https://openalex.org/W4410647264||ABSTRACT||001]. So, the overall link is that green nanotechnology is positioned as a remediation-oriented, sustainable agricultural strategy, and biogenic nanoparticles matter because their biological origins are what many reviews treat as the basis for that sustainability claim [https://openalex.org/W4225104982||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402449485||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the EU Taxonomy relate to global greenhouse gas emissions, and what does the labour force participation study say about reducing those emissions in developing countries?
final_answer: The strongest direct link between the EU Taxonomy and greenhouse gas emissions in the supplied evidence is that it is described as a standardized classification system for sustainable economic activities that covers activities responsible for up to 80% of EU greenhouse gas emissions, with the intended role of channeling investment toward low-carbon technologies [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000]. The same paper cautions that the Taxonomy’s impact depends on how strict its technical performance thresholds are for activities that are not yet "green," and finds that for several sectors those thresholds are not yet sufficient to support a transition to climate neutrality [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, other papers in the set emphasize that greenhouse gas emissions remain a central climate metric and that decarbonization is necessary, but they do not directly connect those claims to the EU Taxonomy [https://openalex.org/W4281764797||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper on global emissions notes that global greenhouse gas emissions are still rising even though 24 countries achieved sustained annual CO2 and GHG reductions between 1970 and 2018, totaling 3.2 GtCO2eq since their peaks [https://openalex.org/W3215792940||ABSTRACT||000]. On the labour-force question, the clearest evidence comes from a panel of 173 countries showing that labour force participation generally improves environmental quality and, in developing countries, rising labour force participation significantly reduces GHG emissions [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000]. That study also reports heterogeneity: labour force participation lowers pollution in low-income and high-income countries, is environment-degrading in upper-middle-income countries, and is insignificant in developed economies [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence suggests the EU Taxonomy is designed as an investment-guidance tool for a large share of EU-emitting activities, while the labour-force study implies that expanding labour force participation may be one pathway to reducing emissions in developing countries, though the effect is not uniform across income groups [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
final_answer: The systematic review says OSC has been shown to improve environmental performance by reducing waste generation and carbon emissions, presenting these as part of its broader environmental savings [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. It also reports that, despite these benefits, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration by 2018 [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The review therefore treats it as timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance because doing so would help extract learnings and strategies from current research and compare what is happening in developed and developing regions [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||001]. This framing is consistent with the review’s broader aim of consolidating knowledge using PRISMA and mapping links among major categories and trends, while also calling for further studies [https://openalex.org/W4385812085||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review summarized in the evidence similarly emphasizes that environmental outcomes can vary by context and that robust evaluation is needed, with positive results occurring in 51% of cases, no difference in 41%, and negative outcomes in 8% [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the evidence supports a generally favorable but not uniformly positive environmental picture for OSC and suggests that the low level of market penetration by 2018 makes understanding success factors especially important [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001].

final_answer: In the Pakistan SMEs study, affective commitment (AC) was used as a mediating mechanism within a single unified framework that linked workplace spirituality (WPS), responsible leadership (RL), and pro-environmental behavior (PEB), and the study tested these relationships using survey data from 390 employees and structural equation modeling (SEM) [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000]. The results indicated significant positive relationships among workplace spirituality, responsible leadership, and pro-environmental behavior, with support for both the direct effects and the mediating role of AC [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000]. In other words, the study suggests that AC helped explain how WPS and RL were connected to stronger pro-environmental behavior in Pakistan’s SMEs [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000]. The authors concluded that integrating workplace spirituality and responsible leadership into business practices may help encourage pro-environmental behavior in Pakistan’s SMEs [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||001]. Related Pakistan-sector studies also support the broader idea that pro-environmental behavior can function as a mediator in sustainability-related models, such as between microlevel CSR and environmental performance in banking [https://openalex.org/W3128452161||ABSTRACT||001] and between responsible leadership and sustainable business performance [https://openalex.org/W4367316216||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, digital tools are portrayed as useful when they are integrated into environmental education in ways that connect knowledge, practice, and sustainability goals [https://openalex.org/W4313362444||ABSTRACT||000]. Several summaries emphasize that technology-supported learning can strengthen environmental education by helping learners build awareness of climate change, biodiversity loss, and other sustainability challenges, while also encouraging behavior change and engagement [https://openalex.org/W2281915808||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4399175475||ABSTRACT||000]. A review of 21 studies found that digital tools in environmental education were associated with environmental learning gains and increased concern for the sustainability of the planet, with virtual reality emerging as the most prominent digital approach and climate change as the most common topic [https://openalex.org/W4396495518||ABSTRACT||000]. The papers also suggest that digital tools work best when paired with pedagogical approaches that are practice-oriented, interdisciplinary, and designed to foster critical thinking, social engagement, and sustainability competences rather than simple lecturing [https://openalex.org/W4361975213||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4210723178||ABSTRACT||001]. One conceptual paper further argues that digital technologies can support sustainable digital learning by organizing knowledge, highlighting sustainability concerns, and guiding future educational practice and research [https://openalex.org/W4361222029||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the literature cautions that digital learning itself raises sustainability concerns and that broader barriers such as resistance to change, insufficient funding, and lack of awareness can limit effective implementation [https://openalex.org/W4361222029||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4361975213||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence points to digital tools fostering sustainability awareness most effectively when they are embedded in active, context-sensitive environmental education that helps learners connect local and global problems to collective action [https://openalex.org/W4399175475||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4311849879||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The clearest description of the 87-study selection process comes from the review that identified those studies in Scopus for 2017–2023 using the keywords “Sustainability assessment” OR “Life cycle assessment” AND “Internal combustion engine*” OR “ICE*,” followed by careful screening [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. That same review says the screened studies were then classified across six aspects: sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies (including alternative fuels), types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review shows a different but related approach: it used the PRISMA protocol, searched scientific databases, and built an evaluation matrix to classify papers according to several integrated criteria [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, the selected set included 84 case studies overall, with 52 stand-alone LCA studies, 8 LCC studies combined with other analyses, and no S-LCA studies [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||001]. The same review indicates that its classification emphasized LCA indicators such as global warming potential, eutrophication, human toxicity, and ecotoxicity, with only a few studies using circular economy indicators [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, two other papers do not provide enough detail to reconstruct screening or categorization rules for 87 studies: one only reports broad journal and keyword restrictions with 144 retrieved articles [https://openalex.org/W4403910234||ABSTRACT||000], and another mentions a systematic selection process for circular economy indicators but no explicit study-selection or classification rules for 87 LCA studies [https://openalex.org/W4388662253||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that selection was typically done through database searching plus screening, while classification schemes varied by review and could focus on sectoral dimensions, integrated sustainability criteria, or indicator categories [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000].

The clearest quantitative biomass result comes from the study summarized at W4390342199, which reports that on a 3-year average Pennisetum glaucum and U. brizantha cv. The broader meta-analysis evidence indicates that legume cover crops increased yield by 16.0% and soil organic carbon by 5.9%, while non-legume cover crops increased soil organic carbon by 4.0% and legume cover crops raised nitrous oxide emissions by 36.2%, but these are aggregated effects rather than site- and year-specific comparisons among individual cover crops [https://openalex.org/W4408217859||ABSTRACT||000]. query: What changes are reshaping the Industrial manufacturing industry, and what should companies focus on to support digital and green transformation?
final_answer: The papers agree that Industrial manufacturing is being reshaped by digital transformation, the digital economy, and Industry 4.0 technologies such as cloud computing, big data, IoT, AI, and internet-based connectivity, which are changing production methods, management models, and innovation capabilities [https://openalex.org/W4313238684||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4319599463||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3164306258||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the evidence, these changes are repeatedly linked to greener outcomes, including more sustainable production, better energy conservation, improved efficiency, and reduced overproduction or underproduction through predictive analytics and supply-chain coordination [https://openalex.org/W4319599463||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4360777148||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers specifically frame green digital transformation as combining digitalization with green technologies so that business processes, products, and models become environmentally sustainable [https://openalex.org/W3182760100||ABSTRACT||001]. The strongest message on what companies should do is to integrate digital and green technologies deliberately, rather than assuming digitalization will automatically produce sustainability benefits [https://openalex.org/W4302303968||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4403107862||ABSTRACT||001]. Companies are also advised to invest in modern manufacturing technologies and the infrastructure needed to operate them, while coordinating transformation across service, model, and organization dimensions to build sustainable innovation capability [https://openalex.org/W4360777148||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313238684||ABSTRACT||001]. Collaboration and policy support are also emphasized, with one paper noting that governments, businesses, and the tech industry should work together and that policy development can help overcome barriers [https://openalex.org/W4403107862||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the literature notes important constraints, including integration challenges, economic and regulatory barriers, and implementation challenges for environmental solutions in manufacturing [https://openalex.org/W4403107862||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4302303968||ABSTRACT||000]. Regional differences also matter: the digital economy’s effect on industrial green transformation is reported as stronger in eastern-central China and weaker in western China, suggesting companies should account for spatiotemporal context when planning transformation [https://openalex.org/W4387972406||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The available summaries point to the DECISION study as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial in patients with locally advanced/metastatic RAI-refractory DTC, designed to test whether sorafenib improves progression-free survival (PFS) [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The ClinicalTrials.gov identifier reported for this trial in the provided evidence is NCT00984282 [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The treatment schedule is described as continuing until radiographically documented disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days (2 cycles), while safety assessments were done every 28 days (1 cycle) for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The primary endpoint was PFS, and secondary endpoints included OS, time to disease progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetic analysis [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Other paper summaries mention DECISION-related registration numbers in different registries or indicate that ClinicalTrials.gov details were not provided, but they do not add additional design or endpoint information for the phase III record [pmc_PMC10387733||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806070||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC5387979||ABSTRACT||002].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: Based on the provided summaries, nano-enhancers appear to be better for workpiece burn mainly because they improve lubrication, cooling, and heat transfer during machining, which helps prevent burn-related surface damage [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. In titanium alloy machining, nano-enhancers with high thermal conductivity are specifically recommended because they improve lubrication and cooling performance and thereby help solve the workpiece burn problem [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. A related review on nano-enhanced biolubricants says their benefits come from better film formation, atomization, infiltration, and anti-friction/heat-transfer mechanisms, and that experimental studies have already verified improved tool wear and surface integrity [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. The same paper suggests that nano-enhancer type, lubricant type, concentration, and micro-droplet size all matter, so the burn-prevention benefit depends on how the nano-enhancer is formulated and delivered [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. The summaries also indicate that nano-enhancers with high hardness and spherical characteristics may be better choices, implying these physical properties contribute to reduced surface burn and grinding issues [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. However, several papers do not discuss workpiece burn or nano-enhancers at all, and some only mention nano-enhancers in very general terms, so the direct evidence base is limited [https://openalex.org/W4322505914||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4324057306||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3196394368||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the strongest support in the provided evidence is that nano-enhancers are better for burn control when they have high thermal conductivity and are used to strengthen lubrication and cooling in machining [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do carbon dots compare with inorganic quantum dots as optical nanomaterials, and what sustainability issues are highlighted in the review?
final_answer: Across the reviews, carbon dots/carbon quantum dots are consistently portrayed as promising optical nanomaterials because they combine luminescence or photoluminescence with low toxicity, biocompatibility, water solubility, photostability, and tunable surface or structural properties [https://openalex.org/W4401798421||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4406866034||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313550231||ABSTRACT||000]. Several reviews also describe them as useful across bioimaging, sensing, photocatalysis, optoelectronics, biomedical devices, and environmental monitoring, underscoring broad application potential [https://openalex.org/W4378391047||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4403909528||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387573993||ABSTRACT||000]. In the papers that do address the comparison conceptually, carbon dots are framed as a functional and sustainable alternative to incumbent optical nanomaterials, notably inorganic quantum dots, largely because they can be made from biomass or other renewable/waste-derived starting materials and can avoid toxic, precious, or critical raw materials [https://openalex.org/W4400778971||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4318483232||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the evidence provided does not supply a direct side-by-side performance comparison with inorganic quantum dots, so the reviews support a qualitative rather than quantitative contrast [https://openalex.org/W4401798421||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313550231||ABSTRACT||000]. The sustainability discussion is strongest around synthesis and feedstocks: authors emphasize green synthesis, biomass-derived precursors, food- or waste-derived carbon sources, eco-friendly methods, and alignment with green chemistry, circular economy, and Safe and Sustainable by Design principles [https://openalex.org/W4406866034||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387573993||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4403909528||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the reviews caution that many reported methods are still not fully sustainable because pretreatment, purification, solvents, energy use, and waste management can be resource-intensive or wasteful [https://openalex.org/W4400778971||ABSTRACT||000]. They also note practical limitations such as low quantum yield, reproducibility problems, heterogeneity, limited scalability, and the need for better standardization and quantitative reporting of material, solvent, and energy requirements [https://openalex.org/W4403909528||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400778971||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the relevant studies, mask mandates appear to help reduce COVID-19 spread by lowering infection incidence and by offsetting some of the increase in cases associated with higher mobility and weaker prevention. In a US state-level analysis, a mask mandate could offset about one third of the increase in case growth caused by a one-standard-deviation rise in mobility, and the estimated effect was stronger in states with higher compliance [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. The same study estimated that a national mask mandate starting on May 15, 2020 would have reduced total US infections by 23.7% to 30.4% by November 15, 2020, indicating a substantial population-level benefit [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study found that keeping prevention measures in place for at least 2 months was associated with lower COVID-19 incidence, and this pattern held for face mask mandates specifically [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. That study also reported that the monthly incidence difference associated with sustained mask mandates ranged from about –4 cases per 100,000 in low-vulnerability counties to –401 cases per 100,000 in high-vulnerability counties, suggesting larger benefit in more socially vulnerable communities [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate indoor-environment study found that a face mask combined with upward ventilation reduced infectious concentration by nearly 99.95% compared with no precautions, but also warned that a mask can be counterproductive if it is placed inappropriately with ventilation, implying that masks work best as part of a proper strategy rather than alone [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Supporting the general protective effect of masks, healthcare-worker studies found that face masks and especially N95 or surgical masks provided significant protection against infection, while gloves, gowns, and some other PPE components showed less clear benefit [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests mask mandates help lower COVID-19 cases, particularly when compliance is high, when they are maintained for longer periods, and when paired with other measures such as ventilation [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) appears in the evidence primarily as a tribologically functional nanoparticle additive in biolubricant research, but only one paper summary clearly states that it was actually used in canola oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000]. In that canola-oil study, hBN was added as a solid nanoparticle additive to improve the oil’s tribological performance, motivated by the fact that canola oil is non-toxic and low-cost but has weaker tribological performance than petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The evaluation included hBN concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% and compared them with graphene nanoplatelet (GNP) formulations, while measuring dynamic viscosity and running coefficient-of-friction and wear tests in the boundary lubrication regime using a pin-on-disk setup [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. For hBN alone, 1.0 wt.% produced the lowest coefficient of friction, reducing it by 40% relative to base oil, and optimized hBN+GNP mixtures reduced friction by 56% and wear by 90% versus base oil, attributed to a protective composite film and polishing mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. Other papers in the set are reviews that mention nanoparticles, two-dimensional films, or h-BN as potential additive classes in sustainable lubricants, but they do not provide canola-oil-specific experimental details [https://openalex.org/W4401870224||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4306936325||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000]. Several summaries explicitly state that they contain no evidence for hBN in canola oil, which limits the broader synthesis to this single experimental study [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4327639096||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3161620664||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests hBN was used as a performance-enhancing additive in canola oil and evaluated through standard tribological and viscosity tests, but the surrounding literature here is largely review-based rather than additional direct experimental confirmation [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the papers, organizational learning capability is portrayed as a pathway that can support radical innovation by improving how organizations process knowledge, experiment, and make decisions. The clearest direct evidence comes from one study showing that organizational learning capability fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, and that it fosters experimentation, dialog, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper similarly describes organizational learning as vital for organizational performance and notes that innovation can be disruptive if it is not well-informed and well-processed, implying that learning helps make innovation more effective [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from the top-management literature also suggests that ambidextrous learning in the TMT is positively associated with adoption of sustainable business model innovations, and that TMT diversity and university-industry collaboration support this learning process [https://openalex.org/W4323928282||ABSTRACT||000]. At a broader conceptual level, organizational learning research emphasizes deeper organizational change, including deutero learning, societal learning scope, and cooperative advantage, which aligns with transformation-oriented innovation even when radical innovation is not named explicitly [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000]. However, several papers do not directly address radical innovation and instead link organizational learning to sustainable performance, sustainable value creation, or innovation capability more generally, so the evidence is not uniform [https://openalex.org/W3211385979||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the synthesis suggests that organizational learning capability contributes to radical innovation mainly by enabling richer knowledge processing, openness to external input, and organizational conditions that support experimentation and strategic change, but the strongest direct evidence is limited to a small number of studies [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4320476375||ABSTRACT||000].

final_answer: The clearest evidence shows that, in Romania, the SDG Index is used as an integrated framework to measure progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals at local and regional level by combining 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. This approach is described as a way to assess sustainable development performance across territories rather than just at the national scale, and it is aligned with broader calls for robust regional data infrastructure and indicator sets that support benchmarking and policy action [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001]. The results showed a strong spatial concentration of the highest sustainable development performance in specific geographical areas, while rural areas and extended peripheral regions in eastern and southern Romania were the poorest performers [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, this suggests the SDG Index can reveal marked internal disparities even when used within a single country at subnational scale [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. No other provided evidence contradicts this Romanian finding, but the other papers mainly discuss indicator frameworks or unrelated SDG applications rather than Romania-specific SDG Index results [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4389430761||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4380487766||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the available evidence supports the SDG Index as a practical local/regional monitoring tool in Romania, but only one Romania-specific study summary is available, so the conclusion is narrow [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What are biomasses converted into through thermochemical decomposition?
final_answer: Across the provided summaries, biomass is most consistently described as being converted through thermochemical decomposition into energy-related outputs, including energy, heat, and biofuels [https://openalex.org/W4400734527||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4320879845||ABSTRACT||001]. Several papers also broaden the product list to include fuels, products, platform molecules, chemicals, and energy vectors, indicating that thermochemical or catalytic biomass decomposition can yield multiple classes of valuable outputs rather than a single product stream [https://openalex.org/W4320879845||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4377108088||ABSTRACT||000]. One review specifically states that thermochemical/catalytic decomposition can convert biomass into a series of biofuels and high-value-added products [https://openalex.org/W4377108088||ABSTRACT||000]. Another summary notes that biomass can be converted into platform molecules and also used to make carbon-based materials or green catalytic supports, although this is described for lignocellulose revalorization more generally rather than as a direct thermochemical product claim [https://openalex.org/W3125494550||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, multiple summaries explicitly say they do not specify the exact products of thermochemical decomposition, so the evidence base is incomplete and the answers are often framed at a high level of abstraction [https://openalex.org/W4400734527||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4320494881||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3139112995||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4367312219||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the papers agree that thermochemical decomposition is a pathway for turning biomass into energy and higher-value bio-based outputs, but they do not provide a single, precise, universally specified product list [https://openalex.org/W4400734527||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4377108088||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How do thermal pwer plants relate to the environmental issues described in the survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing?
final_answer: Across these surveys, the main environmental issues in sustainable cloud computing are high electricity use, carbon emissions, heat generation, cooling demand, water consumption, and electronic waste from data centers and related infrastructure [https://openalex.org/W4385490509||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4385723923||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers treat thermal power plants as part of the broader electricity system behind these impacts, with one survey stating that cloud data centers and equipment consume vast amounts of energy that are “mainly” generated by thermal power plants and that these plants often rely on fossil fuels such as coal and oil [https://openalex.org/W4281251447||ABSTRACT||000]. That same paper explicitly links thermal power plants to global warming, CO2 emissions, ozone layer depletion, and premature deaths, making them a direct contributor to the environmental harms associated with cloud computing’s electricity demand [https://openalex.org/W4281251447||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers are more cautious and do not mention thermal power plants directly, instead framing the problem as data-center energy demand and emissions that should be reduced through energy-efficient techniques such as virtualization, consolidation, cooling improvements, power management, low-power electronics, and thermal management [https://openalex.org/W4385490509||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3172706057||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4385723923||ABSTRACT||001]. Advanced cooling and sustainability approaches are also presented as ways to lower greenhouse gas emissions, energy demand, and blue water consumption in data centers [https://openalex.org/W4410019315||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper further notes that green data-center transition involves integrating renewable energy with fluctuating power grids and using AI and edge computing to optimize cooling and resource use, which suggests an indirect route for reducing reliance on polluting generation sources [https://openalex.org/W4391045525||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the papers agree that the environmental burden comes from electricity-intensive cloud operations, but they differ on whether thermal power plants are named explicitly as the upstream source of that burden or only implied as part of the energy mix [https://openalex.org/W4381251447||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3172706057||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: In hepatocellular carcinoma, macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was reported to be significantly upregulated in both tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line, and its expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and tumor size [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. siRNA-mediated knockdown of MIF inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth rate in an in vivo xenograft model [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. At the protein/signaling level, MIF knockdown increased Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, while decreasing cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. These findings suggest that MIF supports HCC cell growth and survival, whereas reducing MIF shifts cells toward apoptosis and away from proliferation [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. The other supplied papers did not provide additional evidence about MIF in HCC or its knockdown effects, so the synthesis is based on this single relevant study [pmc_PMC10140795||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC3162940||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC4169566||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC4176125||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC4176124||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9194659||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9890137||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10063289||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
final_answer: The supplied evidence indicates that the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction improved over the study period, but the clearest change depended on whether outcomes were assessed at the institutional level or for an individual surgeon [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. At the institution level, the main sign of improvement was a shorter hospital stay in later cases compared with earlier cases, including for both single and double DIEP procedures, while no other statistically significant start-to-end differences were found [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. By contrast, the single-surgeon analysis showed a significant reduction in total surgery time over time, suggesting a more pronounced learning curve when the same operator was tracked longitudinally [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. The other provided papers do not add DIEP-specific learning-curve evidence and explicitly state that they do not address DIEP reconstruction or operative experience over time [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10364779||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364779||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10364871||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364871||ABSTRACT||002]. One additional paper reports longer-term revision and secondary reconstruction rates for breast reconstruction procedures generally, but it does not describe a DIEP learning curve [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests modest institutional improvement over time and a clearer operative-time improvement for a single surgeon, but it does not support a broader or more detailed characterization of the DIEP learning curve beyond those findings [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How cross-disciplinary collaborations help sustainability education for manufacturing teams facing digitalization and skill changes?
final_answer: Cross-disciplinary collaboration appears to help sustainability education by making learning more inclusive, more holistic, and more closely connected to real sustainability challenges [https://openalex.org/W4386284045||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4390432598||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386455762||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the summaries, collaboration is described as supporting social skills such as cooperative work, bringing together diverse academic disciplines, and enabling transdisciplinary learning through social interaction, experience-based collaboration, and societal interaction [https://openalex.org/W4386284045||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4386455762||ABSTRACT||000]. For manufacturing teams facing digitalization and skill changes, the evidence suggests this matters because digitalization is reshaping sustainability education needs, and curricula and workforce development must adapt to new expectations and competencies [https://openalex.org/W4390751453||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4315651657||ABSTRACT||001]. Several papers also indicate that collaboration is especially important when sustainability problems cross organizational boundaries, since transdisciplinary partnerships are used to co-produce knowledge and cross-sector partnerships can support education-related and broader social change [https://openalex.org/W4205707734||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4318833090||ABSTRACT||000]. In digitalized supply-chain settings, sustainability benefits are more likely when firms address digitalization collaboratively, partly because issues like data sharing concerns and rebound effects can otherwise limit gains [https://openalex.org/W4220997944||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence is cautious: the literature says inter- and transdisciplinary sustainability education is still understudied in terms of how collaboration outcomes are evaluated, so there is not yet strong agreement on what works best [https://openalex.org/W4283808475||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4205707734||ABSTRACT||000]. The sources therefore support collaboration as a promising educational and organizational approach for manufacturing teams, but they also show that implementation is constrained by practical barriers and that more follow-up research is needed [https://openalex.org/W3128291854||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4283808475||ABSTRACT||001].

key_claims.claim: Cross-disciplinary and transdisciplinary collaboration can make sustainability education more inclusive, cooperative, and holistic by linking diverse disciplines and social interaction to real-world sustainability challenges [https://openalex.org/W4386284045||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4390432598||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386455762||ABSTRACT||000].
key_claims.notes: The cited chunks explicitly mention educational inclusion, collaborative/cooperative work, convergence of diverse disciplines, holistic learning, social interaction, and solving real-world problems.

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, coronary artery calcification is most consistently presented as a marker of worse cardiovascular risk and complications rather than as a protective finding [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In a trauma cohort of 433 patients, left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with any complication (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.7–8.9), and a greater number of calcified coronary arteries was associated with an adverse discharge condition [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, coronary artery calcification score predicted all-cause mortality over 4.4 years, and sex-, age-, and race/ethnicity-specific percentiles did not outperform absolute CACS for predicting mortality complications [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. A broader review similarly states that coronary artery calcium is associated with future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and improves risk prediction when added to global risk models, although it also notes that screening with CAC has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes or healthcare costs [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. The same review cautions that identical CAC levels may correspond to different absolute ASCVD risks across regions and ethnic groups, suggesting that the complication risk associated with calcification is population-dependent [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In heavily calcified coronary lesions treated with orbital atherectomy, invasive imaging showed substantial plaque modification and the initial experience reported no primary safety events at 30 days, indicating that severe calcification can be managed procedurally with favorable short-term safety in that setting [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. However, several papers in the set do not discuss coronary calcification at all, so the evidence is limited to a small number of studies and specific populations [pmc_PMC10140970||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10141707||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8758654||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9806495||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What is SG in this review?
final_answer: Across the provided reviews, the most defensible reading is that “SG” is not consistently defined and cannot be determined with certainty from most abstracts [https://openalex.org/W4392003298||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3119763312||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4392357391||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4284681716||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4385483133||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4380487766||ABSTRACT||001]. Several papers instead focus on SDGs, ESG, or related abbreviations such as SGI, SCs, SD goals, and SDRs, without explicitly expanding “SG” [https://openalex.org/W4392003298||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3119763312||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4392357391||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4284681716||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4385483133||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4380487766||ABSTRACT||001]. One review does offer the clearest tentative explanation, stating that “SG” appears to refer to the practice of integrating some, but not all, environmental, social, and governance factors to create value [https://openalex.org/W4400205024||ABSTRACT||001]. In that same review, the term is linked to a broader critique of ESG as a label that has been “weaponized” and to a shift from mere incorporation toward prioritization or exclusive consideration of ESG factors [https://openalex.org/W4400205024||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4400205024||ABSTRACT||002]. However, other papers in the set use SDGs positively as a sustainability agenda, a reporting target, or a footprint metric, and one review argues SDGs can also be used symbolically as camouflage for legitimacy [https://openalex.org/W4392003298||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4281686775||ABSTRACT||001]. So, if the question is asking what “SG” means in this review set, the best evidence-based answer is that it is probably a shorthand for selective integration of ESG factors, but this interpretation is only explicitly stated in one abstract and is not confirmed by the others [https://openalex.org/W4400205024||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: The available evidence suggests that KAI1 and VEGF are both individually useful biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and that using them together improves diagnostic performance compared with KAI1 alone [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. In one study, serum KAI1 was downregulated and VEGF was upregulated in HCC, and both markers showed diagnostic value, with AUCs of 0.907 for KAI1 and 0.779 for VEGF [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The combined detection increased sensitivity from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy from 83.06% to 84.68%, while the negative predictive value reached 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study also reported that KAI1 was associated with TNM stage, intrahepatic metastasis, lymph node or peritoneal metastasis, and portal vein thrombus, whereas VEGF was closely related to α-fetoprotein level, which may help explain why the pair adds complementary diagnostic information [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the supplied evidence does not include corroborating studies of KAI1/VEGF combination testing from the other papers, and several summaries explicitly state that they do not address KAI1, VEGF, or HCC diagnosis [pmc_PMC8318739||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9806080||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3178660840||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports combined KAI1 and VEGF testing as a potentially better diagnostic panel than either marker alone, but the conclusion rests on limited data from a single summarized study [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Across the provided papers, the clearest explanation is that microplastics threaten global public health through contaminated fishmeal entering aquaculture feeds and then moving into farmed fish that people eat [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper states that small pelagic and oceanic fish used to make fishmeal accumulate microplastics, and that fishmeal is a primary ingredient in aquaculture and livestock feeds, creating a route for microplastics to enter aquaculture systems through contaminated feed [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. The same paper adds that once in aquaculture, microplastics may interact with pond ecosystems, alter cultured fish physiology and behavior, and accumulate in edible portions, which could cause severe physiological disorders in fish consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. A Bangladesh study strengthens this pathway by reporting that all commercial fish feed samples were contaminated with microplastics, with mean abundances of 500 to 2200 MPs/kg, showing a direct feed-to-fish entry route [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. More generally, several papers agree that microplastics can move through aquatic food chains and contaminate seafood pathways, creating public-health risks for humans who consume fish and seafood [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000]. However, some papers only support indirect environmental concern rather than a fishmeal-specific health mechanism, and one zebrafish study even found no serious toxic effects from polyethylene spheres because there was no internalization, despite changes in AChE and GST activities [https://pmc_PMC9967563||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests the public-health threat is plausible and food-chain mediated, but the fishmeal-specific human-health impact is not well quantified in the provided summaries [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4367322982||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: The Iraq study directly addressed maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination in 1-day-old imported broiler chicks, using 451 Ross 308 chicks from 28 flocks and 256 Cobb 500 chicks from 17 flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Both strains were reported to have high and uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 performed better overall [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Specifically, Cobb 500 had a higher antibody-positive rate than Ross 308 (100% vs 97.78%), a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), and a lower mean CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%) [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. No other provided paper summaries address this specific Iraq/Newcastle disease comparison, so the evidence for strain performance comes from this single study [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10330971||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC4172590||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models help explain adult heart cardiac regeneration by using the brief regenerative window in newborn mice as a biological system to uncover molecular mechanisms that are otherwise limited or absent in adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. The neonatal heart is presented as a key model because it retains full regenerative capacity for a short period after injury, and this may also apply to the neonatal human heart [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. By studying these models, researchers can identify factors that stimulate regeneration through endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which is directly relevant to designing therapies for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. The evidence also frames neonatal injury models as part of a broader strategy, together with large animal and human insights, to support novel regenerative medicine approaches for adult heart disease [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the other provided papers do not address neonatal injury models or adult cardiac regeneration, and instead focus on unrelated topics such as neonatal clinical deterioration monitoring, heart valve implants, LVAD-associated myocardial recovery, or hypertrophic/fibrotic responses in non-neonatal mouse injury/challenge models [pmc_PMC10230358||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10143004||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9806425||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. Therefore, based on the available evidence, the main contribution of neonatal injury models is their role as a mechanistic bridge between naturally regenerative neonatal biology and potential adult heart repair strategies, rather than direct proof of adult regeneration itself [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001].
