query: How can the Paris Agreement be used in makin�27 healthcare or manufacturing teams push more sustainable practices, and what do the three I's say about why policy coherence with it can be helped or hindered?
final_answer: The papers suggest that the Paris Agreement can be used as a policy reference point or signal to push healthcare and, more generally, organizational teams toward more sustainable practices by anchoring coherence efforts in broader climate and sustainability agendas [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3166839458||ABSTRACT||000]. In healthcare, this is linked to decarbonising the health system, using intersectoral policymaking, and aligning health policy with environmental goals and social determinants of health [https://openalex.org/W3128473151||ABSTRACT||002]. Another healthcare example is clinical laboratories being encouraged to choose safer and more sustainable alternatives to hazardous chemicals, address sustainability issues, and implement official guidelines to reduce their carbon footprint [https://openalex.org/W4312064827||ABSTRACT||001]. For manufacturing and industry, the evidence is broader but similar: comprehensive chemical legislation is described as a way to transform industry and attract investment into safe and sustainable products and production methods, and sustainable technologies should continue to be developed and implemented despite difficulty [https://openalex.org/W4312064827||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4313495531||ABSTRACT||000]. On policy coherence, the Paris Agreement can be studied alongside other major agendas, and coherence depends on how actors and institutions apply it and whose ideas and interests are served [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000]. The three I’s are ideas, institutions, and interests, and the paper says they shape policy options and the ambition given to agendas and actors, so they can help coherence when they support alignment and hinder it when vested interests or ideologies obstruct it [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the papers, helping factors include sustained implementation, intersectoral coordination, stronger linkages to international agreements, and the use of policy frameworks to reinforce sustainability ambitions [https://openalex.org/W4313495531||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412423688||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||001]. Hindrances include the long-term nature of greenhouse-gas emissions, the benefits of fossil fuels, risk-handling behavior, and tensions or contradictions within and between goals that make alignment harder [https://openalex.org/W4313495531||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412423688||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the review link green nanotechnology with environmental remediation in agro-ecosystems, and why does it say biogenic nanoparticles matter for this?
final_answer: Across the reviews, green nanotechnology is linked to environmental remediation in agro-ecosystems as an eco-friendly, sustainability-oriented alternative to conventional inputs and cleanup methods [https://openalex.org/W4402449485||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225104982||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers describe it as useful for reducing reliance on chemical fungicides and other hazardous substances, improving crop protection, and supporting sustainable agriculture through applications such as fertilizers, pesticides, biosensors, and nano-remediators [https://openalex.org/W4402449485||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000]. Other reviews broaden this to pollution abatement, water treatment, soil quality improvement, and monitoring or detection of metals and organic toxins in farmland systems [https://openalex.org/W4403849839||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225104982||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper goes further and says green nanotechnology should be integrated with conventional remediation techniques, using biosynthesis plus advanced engineering tools and real-time monitoring for restoration and pollution management [https://openalex.org/W4410647264||ABSTRACT||001]. The reviews generally agree that the appeal of green nanotechnology is that it can reduce environmental harm while improving efficiency, productivity, and crop health in agro-ecosystems [https://openalex.org/W4380075578||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000]. Biogenic nanoparticles matter in this framing because they are repeatedly presented as more sustainable, biocompatible, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly than physically or chemically synthesized nanoparticles, which are described as harmful, non-economical, or less sustainable [https://openalex.org/W4380075578||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390194078||ABSTRACT||000]. They are also important because the reviews connect them to practical agro-ecosystem functions such as nanofertilizers, agrochemical carriers, biocontrol, soil health management, and remediation of crop and human pathogens [https://openalex.org/W4380075578||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4324149138||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402449485||ABSTRACT||000]. query: How does TSignal handle SPs, and what does it predict about their cleavage site and presence on benchmark datasets?
final_answer: TSignal is described as a deep transformer-based neural network that uses BERT language models and dot-product attention to predict signal peptides (SPs), which are short N-terminal amino acid segments involved in protein translocation and then cleaved off [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. It predicts both whether an SP is present and where the cleavage site lies between the SP and the mature protein [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. On common benchmark datasets, TSignal is reported to achieve competitive accuracy for SP presence prediction and state-of-the-art accuracy for cleavage-site prediction for most SP types and organism groups [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. The abstract also says the model identifies useful biological information on heterogeneous test sequences [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. No provided evidence from the other summaries adds contradictory information about TSignal, but those papers do not mention TSignal or SPs at all, so they cannot independently confirm or refine its SP-handling behavior or benchmark performance [pmc_PMC10311303||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4391385008||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the available evidence supports that TSignal both detects SPs and predicts their cleavage sites, with especially strong benchmark results for cleavage-site prediction [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the EU Taxonomy relate to global greenhouse gas emissions, and what does the labour force participation study say about reducing those emissions in developing countries?
final_answer: The strongest direct evidence on the EU Taxonomy says it is a standardized classification of sustainable economic activities and that it covers activities responsible for up to 80% of EU greenhouse gas emissions, so it is presented as a major tool for steering investment toward low-carbon technologies [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000]. However, that same summary cautions that in several sectors the current thresholds are not yet on track to support climate neutrality, which limits how fully the Taxonomy can deliver emissions reductions on its own [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, the other EU-related studies reinforce the idea that green investment and renewable-energy transitions are associated with lower emissions in Europe: one paper reports that the EU has used green investments to support a low-carbon transition and has set goals of at least a 40% GHG reduction by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050 [https://openalex.org/W4386048713||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386048713||ABSTRACT||001], while another finds that in Central and Eastern European EU countries increased renewable energy shares have been accompanied by reduced greenhouse gas emissions [https://openalex.org/W3128252787||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, there is a warning that reliance on unstable renewables such as photovoltaics and wind can create new sustainability challenges because of supply instability and dispersion [https://openalex.org/W3128252787||ABSTRACT||000]. For the labour-force-participation part of the query, the relevant study reports that higher labour force participation significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions in developing countries, while the effect is insignificant in developed economies [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000]. It further states that this relationship is heterogeneous across income groups: labour force participation reduces pollution in low-income and high-income countries but is environment-degrading in upper-middle-income countries [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence suggests that EU climate policy tools are aimed at a large share of emissions and may support decarbonization, but the labour-force study indicates that in developing countries social and economic participation may also be an emissions-reducing channel [https://openalex.org/W4200364028||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387873299||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
final_answer: The systematic review on OSC says that OSC has enhanced environmental performance, specifically by reducing waste generation and carbon emissions, which it presents as a key benefit of OSC [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. It also reports that by 2018 no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration, despite those environmental benefits [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The review argues that it is timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance because comparing learnings, strategies, differences, similarities, and critical success factors across developed and developing regions can help increase OSC adoption and improve environmental performance [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||001]. This timing is further supported by the broader literature’s emphasis that evidence on sustainability impacts is context dependent and that robust measurement and cross-study synthesis are still needed [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence base remains limited because the provided summaries do not supply the full review details, and one other paper only confirms that its own abstract does not address OSC-specific questions [https://openalex.org/W4385812085||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the review frames OSC as environmentally beneficial but still under-penetrated in markets, making the identification of transferable success factors across regions an important and time-sensitive research task [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did the study use Affective commitment in the framework, and what results it give about workplace spirituality, responsible leadership, and pro-environmental behavior in Pakistan SMEs?
final_answer: In the Pakistan SME study, affective commitment (AC) was used as a mediating mechanism within one unified framework linking workplace spirituality (WPS), responsible leadership (RL), and pro-environmental behavior (PEB), and the model was tested with SEM on survey data from 390 employees in Pakistani SMEs [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000]. The study reported significant positive relationships among WPS, RL, and PEB, supporting both the direct links among these variables and the mediating role of AC [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000]. It further concluded that integrating workplace spirituality and responsible leadership into business practices may encourage pro-environmental behavior in Pakistan’s SMEs [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the other Pakistan-based SME studies provided, the broader pattern is consistent with pro-environmental behavior or environmental sustainability being shaped by organizational practices and context, such as micro-level CSR positively influencing employees’ PEB in healthcare and medium/large firms, and weak finance, education, and government support constraining sustainability adoption in Balochistan SMEs [https://openalex.org/W3133017979||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4396948737||ABSTRACT||000]. However, none of those other summaries mention AC, WPS, or RL, so the evidence for the specific mediation framework comes only from the Pakistan SME study on WPS, RL, and PEB [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3133017979||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4396948737||ABSTRACT||000]. Related work in Pakistan’s banking sector also shows that pro-environmental conduct can operate as a mediator in sustainability models, including a partial mediating role between responsible leadership and sustainable business performance, which is directionally consistent with the idea that employee behavior links leadership or organizational practices to sustainability outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4367316216||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the available evidence is limited because the studies differ in sector, design, and constructs, and only one summary directly reports AC as the mediator in the WPS-RL-PEB framework [https://openalex.org/W4385633441||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4367316216||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?
final_answer: Across the papers, digital tools in environmental education are presented as a way to strengthen sustainability awareness by making learning more engaging, connected to real-world issues, and oriented toward action [https://openalex.org/W4396495518||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313362444||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W2281915808||ABSTRACT||000]. A review of 21 articles found that digital tools were used to promote environmental learning gains and increase concern for the sustainability of the planet, with virtual reality and climate change topics emerging as especially common applications [https://openalex.org/W4396495518||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, another review argues that ICT in education can support sustainable development and the SDGs when used appropriately, especially by linking theoretical and practical research with SDG-oriented practices [https://openalex.org/W4313362444||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers suggest that sustainability awareness is strengthened when learning is not limited to lecturing but instead uses practice-oriented, interdisciplinary, and holistic approaches that fit different learners and contexts [https://openalex.org/W4210723178||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4361975213||ABSTRACT||000]. Digital or technology-supported environmental education is also described as a strategic tool for raising awareness and influencing behavior at school, university, community, and institutional levels, often alongside curricular and policy efforts [https://openalex.org/W2281915808||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4399175475||ABSTRACT||000]. The papers converge on the idea that these tools work best when they support knowledge, skills, values, critical thinking, and collective action rather than simply delivering information [https://openalex.org/W4361975213||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225305823||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence also warns that digital learning itself raises sustainability concerns, and that effective implementation depends on teacher training, funding, stakeholder involvement, and overcoming resistance to change [https://openalex.org/W4361222029||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4361975213||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What converter efficiency, harmonic distortion, or grid-integration stability metrics were reported for the reviewed wind-energy control strategies?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, the evidence provides very few quantitative metrics for wind-energy control strategies, and most abstracts explicitly do not report converter efficiency, harmonic distortion, or numerical grid-integration stability values [https://openalex.org/W4396680626||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4312639565||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4321601607||ABSTRACT||000]. query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The provided evidence does not fully identify the screening criteria or classification rules for the 87 life cycle assessment studies, but it does show that one review located them by searching Scopus for 2017–2023 using the keywords “Sustainability assessment” OR “Life cycle assessment” AND “Internal combustion engine*” OR “ICE*,” followed by careful screening [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001].
